ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let the sign function of the straight line be F(x,y)=3x-2y-a. Substituting the point P=(-3,-1), we get F(P)=3×(-3)-2×(-1)-a=-9+2-a=-7-a. Substituting the point Q=(4,-6), we get F(Q)=3×4-2×(-6)-a=12+12-a=24-a. The two points being on two sides of the straight line is equivalent to the two sign function values having opposite signs, so it is required that (-7-a)(24-a)<0. The two critical values of this inequality are a=-7 and a=24, and solving gives -7<a<24. The endpoints cannot be taken, because the endpoints would make one of the points lie on the straight line, rather than on two sides.

Points on opposite sides of a line have function values with opposite signs, so require (-7-a)(24-a)<0. Solve this inequality to get -7<a<24, with endpoints excluded because an endpoint would put one point on the line rather than on a side.

method.method_draft: View the family of lines as level sets. Rewrite the line as 3x-2y=a and compute the level value h(x,y)=3x-2y at the two given points. For (-3,-1), h=-9+2=-7; for (4,-6), h=12+12=24. A line h=a separates the two points exactly when its level value lies strictly between the two endpoint levels, equivalently when it intersects the open segment joining the points. Therefore a must satisfy -7<a<24.
